cues.en: So what did you think of the sampling method in this video?
cues.zh: 你覺得這支影片的抽樣方法如何？

cues.en: It runs the risk of sampling the same data repeatedly, and it can also completely miss parts of the data just by chance.
cues.zh: 有重複抽到相同資料的風險，也可能碰巧完全漏掉某些部分。

cues.en: But there is less code overall, so it's easier and lighter to implement.
cues.zh: 但整體程式較少，更容易、更輕量地實作。

cues.en: The thing is that if you have a limited data set, you really want to use all available data, but written language isn't like that.
cues.zh: 如果資料集有限，確實會想用所有資料，但書面語言不同。

cues.en: There's just so much text freely available online, so the potential risks of random sampling are overall
cues.zh: 網路免費文字太多，所以隨機抽樣的潛在風險，整體上

cues.en: less compared to, you know, training a CNN to recognize tumors in CT scans.
cues.zh: 比訓練 CNN 從 CT 掃描辨識腫瘤等情況小。

cues.en: The second point is one I've mentioned a few times already, but I do find it very striking.
cues.zh: 第二點之前說過幾次，但仍覺得很驚人。

cues.en: The model had such a tiny amount of data and so few training epochs, and yet it's so quickly just kind of got the gist of what language looks like.
cues.zh: 資料這麼少、訓練週期這麼少，模型卻很快掌握語言的大致樣貌。

cues.en: It wasn't really coherent text, but the spacing, the new lines, some punctuation, context relevant words instead of just random tokens.
cues.zh: 雖然不連貫，但空格、換行、一些標點，以及與上下文相關的字詞，取代了純粹隨機詞元。

cues.en: It really learned a lot about the basic structure and appearance of text with so little data so quickly.
cues.zh: 用這麼少資料、這麼快，就學到許多文字基本結構與樣貌。

cues.en: So I find that to be very interesting.
cues.zh: 我覺得很有意思。
